title: Quantum Model of Computation
question: How do the postulates become a procedure that answers a question?

title: What does a computation consist of?
steps: Choose an input state \(\ket{\psi_{\mathrm{in}}}\) that encodes the question.
Apply unitary steps, together one unitary \(U\).
Measure: one result \(y\) per run, with probability \(|\text{amplitude}|^2\).
Naming \(U\) says nothing about how it is built, or what it costs.

title: Can a step that changes no probability matter?
steps: After the first \(H\): probabilities \(\tfrac12,\tfrac12\). \(Z\) leaves them unchanged.
The relative sign, invisible in the middle, decides the answer.
notes: Gates combine by the matrix product, the later gate on the left: U = U_T ⋯ U_2 U_1.

title: What does one run return, and what does it cost?
steps: Correct with probability 3/4? Repeat and take the most frequent answer; each repetition costs again.
Count qubits, gates, layers, repetitions, preparation, and readout.
One qubit cannot show a speedup: that needs tasks of growing size.

title: Single-Qubit Computation
question: Can one qubit carry out a complete computation?

title: How do we write a program?
takeaway: A wire follows a qubit through time; boxes are gates; M is a measurement; a double line carries a classical bit.

title: Computing NOT with interference
takeaway: At 0 the contributions \(+\tfrac12\) and \(-\tfrac12\) cancel; at 1 they add to one.

title: What if we look in the middle?
question: Insert a measurement after the first H. What does the program output now?
answer: The state becomes |0⟩ or |1⟩, and Z then H give each answer half the time. Both the relative sign and the absence of a measurement are needed.

title: Between no sign change and a full one
takeaway: The last gate turns a phase no measurement could see into the probabilities of the answer.

title: Pauli Operators
question: How many single-qubit operations are there, and can a few describe them all?

title: An operation that exchanges and flips sign
steps: \(ZX=-XZ\): a product of Paulis is a Pauli times a phase.

title: Can four matrices describe every operator?
steps: But a circuit multiplies gates; it does not add them. No Pauli circuit turns \(\ket0\) into \(H\ket0\).
takeaway: Describing an operator is not the same as building it from gates.

title: What we found
items: A computation is an input state, unitary steps, and a measurement read as an answer.
A relative phase invisible in the middle can decide the result.
Cost counts gates, qubits, layers, repetitions, and readout.
One qubit runs a full computation; the phase gate sets its output probabilities.
I, X, Y, Z describe every single-qubit operator, but building gates is a separate question.
